content: BOINC's approach to cross-platform floating-point result verification: exact bitwise agreement across heterogeneous hardware is not pursued; instead BOINC supplies application-specific validator functions with numeric tolerances, and additionally offers 'homogeneous redundancy' (grouping equivalence classes of hardware/software where bitwise agreement IS expected) as a separate mechanism from cross-hardware tolerance -- conflating the two (using a single loose tolerance for both same-class and cross-class comparison) is an anti-pattern; tolerance should be tightest for known-similar hardware classes.
